title: The First Letter to Timothy
lead: A letter in Paul's name to his coworker Timothy, left in Ephesus to stop false teaching and to set the church's life in order: prayer, men and women in worship, overseers and deacons, widows, elders, slaves and the rich. It is one of the three Pastoral Letters, and its authorship and its words on women are among the most debated in the New Testament.

sections.b: After the greeting, Paul charges Timothy to stop teachers busy with myths and genealogies, and remembers the mercy shown to himself, the "first" of sinners (chapter 1). Then come instructions for the church at prayer, for men and for women (chapter 2), the qualities of overseers and deacons, and the church as "household of God" with a short hymn to Christ (chapter 3), a warning about teachers who forbid marriage and foods, and a charge to Timothy himself (chapter 4), the care of widows and the honor and discipline of elders (chapter 5), and slaves, false teachers who seek gain, the danger of the love of money, and a last charge (chapter 6).
sections.refs: 1 Timothy 1:3-20; 1 Timothy 2:1-15; 1 Timothy 3:1-16; 1 Timothy 4:1-16; 1 Timothy 5:1-25; 1 Timothy 6:1-21

sections.h: Why it matters to the churches
sections.b: Few chapters have shaped church life as much: 2:4 in the debates on election, 2:5 on Christ the one mediator, 2:11-15 on women's teaching and leadership, 3:1-13 on church offices and married clergy, 4:14 on ordination, 6:10 on money. The book page and the chapter pages set out the churches' views on each.
